title: Every list endpoint across evidence, audit, vendor, risk, and trust-vault modules enforces a server-side page-size cap
description: Cross-module audit of pagination: evidence.controller.js:114-119 (listEvidence) and vendor-service's ClientVendorRepository.findClientVendors (:315-357, $facet-based) are correctly paginated. audit-assurance.controller.js:478-484 parses page/limit with parseInt() but applies no upper-bound clamp, so ?limit=999999 still returns the full collection. vendor-service's own BaseRepository.findPaginated (BaseRepository.ts:69-99) clamps limit to Math.min(100, ...), but ClientVendorRepository bypasses that helper entirely with a custom pipeline, so the same service has inconsistent enforcement. risk-management-service's RiskRepository.findByOrganization (risk.repository.ts:628-658) and trust-vault-service's CertificationService.list (CertificationService.ts:322-350) do clamp via a pagination options default of {page:1, limit:20}.
preconditions: API test client with ability to override page/limit query params arbitrarily
steps: Call GET /api/audits?limit=999999 and record the number of documents returned
Call the vendor-service client-vendors list endpoint with an equivalently oversized limit
Call the equivalent risk-management-service and trust-vault-service list endpoints with an oversized limit
Compare actual returned document counts against each service's intended page-size cap
expectedResult: risk-management-service and trust-vault-service reject/clamp the oversized limit to their configured default (20). vibrantix-backend's audit endpoint and vendor-service's client-vendors endpoint currently return unbounded result sets for an oversized limit — flag both as gaps requiring a shared server-side clamp (e.g. Math.min(limit, 100)).

title: Mapping workflow-history endpoint performs one findById per history entry with no upstream limit
description: getMappingWorkflowHistory (evidence-mapping.controller.js:1339-1345) queries WorkflowEntry.find({entityType, entityId}).sort().populate('changedBy',...).lean() with no .limit()/.skip() at all, then at :1348-1350 runs await Promise.all(history.map(async (entry) => { ... ClientUser.findById(entry.metadata.assignedTo, ...) })) — one findById per entry. A mapping with a long workflow history (many status changes over its lifetime) amplifies both an unbounded fetch and an N+1 lookup in the same request.
preconditions: A single evidence-control mapping with 200+ WorkflowEntry history records accumulated over time
steps: Call GET .../mappings/:id/workflow-history for the seeded mapping
Capture Mongoose query count and total request duration via the slowQueryMonitor / query profiler
Compare against an equivalent request where history is capped at 50 entries
expectedResult: The uncapped request issues 1 (history fetch) + N (one findById per entry) queries and duration scales linearly with history size. Flag as a gap: the endpoint should cap history length and batch-resolve assignedTo via a single $in query instead of per-entry findById (the codebase already has this batching pattern elsewhere, e.g. evidence-mapping.controller.js:824-916).

title: Role permission changes invalidate the Redis authz cache immediately across concurrent user sessions
description: loadPermissions.js reads via getAuthzCache (redis.js:64-95, key authz:{orgId}:{userId}, TTL 1800s default). role.controller.js calls invalidateOrg() on role update (line 185) and delete (line 242); user.controller.js calls invalidateUser() at multiple points (lines 593, 643, 683, 802, 905). This is a positive control worth an integration regression guard, since the equivalent dashboard KPI cache (dashboard-cache.js) has no such invalidation wired (see PERF-PERF-003) and the two systems should not be confused.
preconditions: User A logged in with an active session and a warm authz cache entry
Admin able to modify User A's role permissions
steps: As User A, call an endpoint gated by permission X and confirm success (cache now warm)
As an admin, revoke permission X from User A's role
Immediately (within the same second) as User A, call the same endpoint again
expectedResult: The second call is rejected with 403 immediately after the role change, confirming invalidateOrg()/invalidateUser() correctly evicts the stale Redis authz cache entry rather than waiting out the 1800s TTL.

title: Organization.findById executes on every authenticated request even when the Redis authz cache hits
description: loadPermissions.js:155 runs Organization.findById(...) unconditionally, ahead of and independent from the getAuthzCache check at line 175 — this DB round trip is not covered by the Redis authz cache, so it fires on literally every authenticated request regardless of cache hit/miss.
preconditions: Warm Redis authz cache entry for a test user
Ability to instrument/count Mongoose queries per request (e.g. via slowQueryMonitor plugin or a query-count middleware)
steps: Warm the authz cache for a test user with one request
Issue 100 subsequent requests as the same user within the TTL window
Count Organization.findById invocations across the 100 requests
expectedResult: Organization.findById is called on all 100 requests despite a cache hit on every one of them. Flag as a gap: the organization lookup should be folded into the authz cache payload or given its own short-TTL cache to avoid a guaranteed per-request DB round trip.

title: Regenerating a report invalidates its cached result before the next fetch
description: report_cache.py (audit-report-generator-service) sets cached reports with a 2h TTL keyed by sha256(audit_id:type:format) (line 148). invalidate() is wired from the regenerate endpoint (routes/reports.py:409). This is the working counterpart to the dashboard KPI cache gap (PERF-PERF-003) and should be guarded as a regression baseline.
preconditions: A previously generated audit report cached from a prior request
steps: Call GET /reports/:auditId to warm the cache
Call the regenerate endpoint for the same audit/type/format
Immediately call GET /reports/:auditId again
expectedResult: The post-regenerate fetch returns the newly generated report content, not the stale cached version — confirming invalidate() correctly evicts the sha256-keyed cache entry.

title: Org+project-scoped audit scope-item queries across audits use a compound index rather than falling back to per-audit compounds
description: audit-scope-item.model.js:380-388 indexes are all scoped to auditId first ({auditId, isDeleted}, {auditId, assessmentStatus}, etc). organizationId and projectId (lines 230-231) are individually indexed but have no compound index together or with assessmentStatus, so a cross-audit query filtered by organizationId+projectId+status (e.g. an org-wide open-items report) cannot use an efficient compound index.
preconditions: Organization with 50+ audits and 10,000+ AuditScopeItem documents across them
steps: Run an explain() on a query filtering AuditScopeItem by {organizationId, projectId, assessmentStatus} without an auditId filter
Inspect the winning plan's index usage
expectedResult: Document whether the query uses an IXSCAN on a suitable compound index or falls back to a COLLSCAN / inefficient index intersection. Flag for remediation (add {organizationId:1, projectId:1, assessmentStatus:1}) if no compound index is used.

title: Evidence pipeline queue chain (ingest -> validate -> normalize -> deduplicate -> store -> map -> risk-notify) completes without job loss when one stage is saturated
description: vibrantix-connector-service defines 7 chained queues plus webhook and drive-upload (src/queues/index.ts:23-45) with per-stage concurrency (ingest=5, validate=10, normalize=10, deduplicate=10, store=5, map=10, risk-notify=1). pipeline.worker.ts wires on('failed') (line 1692) and on('stalled') (line 1740) for the main pipeline stages, but webhook.worker.ts only wires on('failed') (line 134) with no on('stalled') handler.
preconditions: Ability to artificially saturate the evidence-risk-notify queue (conc=1)
steps: Submit 300 evidence items through the full pipeline within a short window
Deliberately saturate evidence-risk-notify by holding its single worker on a slow job
Confirm upstream stages (store, map) continue completing and jobs queue rather than fail
Separately, force a stall condition on a webhook job and confirm whether it is detected/retried
expectedResult: Upstream stages queue jobs at evidence-risk-notify without dropping or failing them (backpressure, not data loss). The webhook stall scenario is NOT detected/retried since webhook.worker.ts has no on('stalled') handler — flag this as a monitoring gap versus the pipeline worker's parity.
